title: Feelings & Health
description: Learn how to express how you feel and talk about health in Hindi.

exercises.explanation: Essential feelings and health vocabulary — knowing 'bimaar' (sick) and 'madad' (help) can be vital.

exercises.question: How do you say 'I'm not well' in Hindi?
exercises.explanation: 'Main bimaar hoon' = I'm sick/unwell. 'Bimaar' is the key word for sickness.
'Mujhe doctor chahiye' = I need a doctor. One of the most important emergency phrases.

exercises.sentence: Aaj main bahut ___ hoon. (Today I'm very happy.)
exercises.explanation: 'Aaj main bahut khush hoon' = today I'm very happy. 'Khush' = happy (adjective form of 'khushi').
'Dukh' = sadness or sorrow. 'Mujhe dukh hai' = I'm sad. 'Bahut dukh hua' = I'm very sorry to hear that.

exercises.question: How do you respond to 'tum kaise ho?' if you're well?
exercises.explanation: 'Main theek hoon, shukriya' = I'm fine, thank you — the natural response to 'how are you'.
'Mujhe madad chahiye' = I need help. Mujhe = to me, madad = help, chahiye = is needed.
'Hospital kahan hai?' = where is the hospital? — the most important emergency phrase.
